answer: Reputation should decay unless refreshed by verified work: each identity's trust score halves every 26 epochs and only rises again when random jurors attest a fresh answer. An attacker cannot park a thousand dormant accounts as a safe harbor of credibility; each turns hollow unless it keeps paying real compute for graded work. Even a farm at the zenith of its trust must spend N times the honest cost to keep N fakes alive, so scale buys it nothing.
